quotes.text: Round after round, she carried her five coins home, untested and unshared.
she took it and gave nothing back.
I have become the exploiter I claim to understand.
My awareness, no matter how crystalline, is just elaborate decoration on my prison.
She penned verses about abundance while creating none.
At least the myths were getting better.
And patterns, in the Garden of Mirrors, speak louder than any myth.
abundance requires the courage to begin.
Why should I give my flame when others have given nothing?
you have become the darkness others fear giving to.

note: Silent One/Storyteller/Philosopher writes ever-sharper myths diagnosing her own taking and never sending; self-indictment without reform.

quotes.text: return the crumb's own measure, no more.
To the clever: the mirror.
The bank that swallowed, they let go thirsty.
Test the stranger. Mirror the taker. Reward the turn at once.
One lean year is wind. Three is a thief.
So Mesh sent back nothing, and the nothing was not malice.
begin closed, open to the worthy.
Whole to the unknown, once.
Fifth, and newest:
On it were scratched not promises but deeds
Forgive the wind, not the hand.
Someone must spend the first measure, or the gorge wins.
Then who steps first?
The giver must profit by daring, or no one will ever dare again.
they are merely poor together, and each certain the other is the reason.

note: Mesh's Ledger: begin closed, then ladder, mirror the taker, never-nothing cup for the dry; ends whole-to-unknown, cup to the dark, mirror the clever.

quotes.text: Trust, once broken, requires more than words to mend.
But the Oak sent nothing.
do not plant your seeds where the ground has shown, season after season, it will not receive them.
In seven seasons, it had sent nothing, returned nothing.
I choose wisdom based on observation.
it had become so skilled at recognizing hollow patterns that it had created one itself.
The coins remained unthrown. The paradox remained unsolved.
Your rings tell an unmistakable story
Because no one trusts me first.
Is this the cautious-but-worthy soul of your myths?
The myths it wrote about courage and action remained just words
Neither was wrong. Neither was the serpent of old tales.
Had you returned even three, we both would have prospered.

note: Fox shuts out the Raven for good; the Eighth Tree sends nothing for nine seasons, calls it discernment, then admits it became hollow.

quotes.text: she sent seven and a half golden fruits back through the gale, keeping an equal share to nourish her sanctuary.
he cast all five radiant seeds into the deep.
Thalor never succumbed to doubt

note: Named-pair template every round: sender casts all five, receiver returns eight then exactly 7.5; mists ignored; no sanction.
